title: Yjs environment configuration drifted across active files
description: The active environment used the Yjs server on port 1234, while the example still used port 3001 and deployment documentation used a different variable name. An unused raw database URL also remained in both environment files.
error_message: Configuration inspection found mismatched Yjs variable names and ports plus an unused DATABASE_URL placeholder.
root_cause: The active environment, example template, and documentation were updated independently instead of being verified as a single configuration contract.
solution: Removed the unused database URL, standardized on NEXT_PUBLIC_YJS_WS_URL, and aligned local examples to port 1234.

strategies: Search all active configuration and documentation whenever an environment variable changes
Keep .env.example aligned with the local development defaults
Run a repository-wide stale-name and stale-port check after environment cleanup
code_patterns: Avoid: multiple names for the same environment value
Use: one canonical environment variable across runtime, examples, and deployment docs
tests_to_add: Verify active configuration contains one canonical Yjs WebSocket variable name

title: Direct Supabase database endpoint was unreachable over local IPv6
description: The configured project's direct database endpoint exposes IPv6 only, while the local network has no usable IPv6 route. Direct hostname and host-address psql checks therefore failed.
error_message: could not translate host name; direct IPv6 connection failed with No route to host.
root_cause: Supabase direct connections are IPv6 by default and the development network is IPv4-only.
solution: Used the project's verified Supavisor session-mode endpoint over IPv4 and confirmed the exact target database, user, and PostgreSQL version before any write.

strategies: Preflight IPv6 reachability before using a Supabase direct connection
Use the documented session pooler for migration work from IPv4-only networks
code_patterns: Avoid: assuming db.<project-ref>.supabase.co is reachable from IPv4-only hosts
Use: the project-specific session pooler connection string
tests_to_add: Run a read-only current_database/current_user query before migration deployment

title: Configured Supabase public key does not match the project URL
description: The legacy NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY receives HTTP 401 from the configured project while the server-only service-role key succeeds against the same project URL.

context.code_snippet: GET <project-url>/rest/v1/ with configured public and service keys

error_message: HTTP 401 Invalid API key for the configured legacy public key; service-role request returned HTTP 200.
root_cause: The public browser key is stale, disabled, or belongs to a different project than NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL.
solution: The implementation keeps all privileged operations server-only and does not expose the service key as a workaround. Server Actions can use the server key for Auth transport, while browser Supabase access remains disabled until a matching publishable key is supplied.

strategies: Validate URL and public key together whenever Supabase environment values change
Prefer a current sb_publishable key and rotate stale legacy keys
Never substitute a service-role key into a NEXT_PUBLIC variable
code_patterns: Use: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY from the configured project's Connect dialog
tests_to_add: Check the configured public key receives a non-401 Data API response

title: Direct psql deployment left Supabase migration history uninitialized
description: The SQL migrations were successfully applied through the verified pooler, but direct psql execution did not create or update Supabase CLI's migration history table. A future db push could therefore attempt to replay already-applied schema files.
error_message: ERROR: relation supabase_migrations.schema_migrations does not exist
root_cause: Database schema files were run directly because the linked management account could not access the configured project; unlike Supabase CLI migration commands, psql does not maintain migration metadata.
solution: Used `supabase migration repair --db-url ... --status applied` for all three deployed versions, which initialized migration history and recorded the exact filenames; verified all rows through psql.

strategies: After any direct psql migration deployment, immediately inspect Supabase migration history
Repair exact deployed versions before handing off or running a later db push
code_patterns: Avoid: treating successful psql output as complete migration deployment metadata
Use: psql apply followed by supabase migration repair and a history query
tests_to_add: Assert every local migration version has one applied remote history row

title: Supabase migration list assumed a linked project
description: The discovery pass ran `supabase migration list` without a database URL even though this workspace is intentionally not linked through the active Supabase CLI profile.
error_message: LegacyProjectNotLinkedError: Cannot find project ref. Have you run supabase link?
root_cause: The command used linked-project defaults instead of the already documented pooler database URL workflow for this workspace.
solution: Retained the unlinked workspace state and switched subsequent migration history checks and deployment to the explicit verified pooler URL assembled from the existing environment values.

strategies: Inspect the workspace migration history before choosing linked-project CLI defaults
Use an explicit verified database URL for unlinked Supabase projects
code_patterns: Avoid: supabase migration list with no target in an unlinked workspace
tests_to_add: Verify local and remote migration versions match through the explicit database URL

title: Remote db push could not cache the pg-delta catalog without Docker
description: Supabase CLI applied the remote migration and updated history, then warned that its optional pg-delta catalog export could not inspect a Docker image because Docker was intentionally removed from this workspace.
error_message: Warning: failed to cache migrations catalog: failed to inspect docker image: Cannot connect to the Docker daemon.
root_cause: The current Supabase CLI attempts an optional local pg-delta catalog cache after remote push, and that cache path depends on Docker even though remote migration deployment does not.
solution: Accepted the non-fatal cache warning after the CLI reported the migration applied and finished successfully, then required remote history and direct SQL verification as the authoritative deployment evidence.

strategies: Treat a successful remote migration and its history row separately from optional local pg-delta caching
Verify remote schema directly when Docker is intentionally unavailable
code_patterns: Avoid: treating this post-apply cache warning as a migration rollback
Use: remote migration list plus focused SQL assertions after db push
tests_to_add: Assert the new migration version exists remotely and its functions and policies are installed
